title: Engine cranks but will not start
shortDescription: Starter spins the flywheel but the engine never fires.
fullDescription:
Briggs & Stratton small engines on mowers, generators, and pressure washers commonly fail to start after sitting with stale fuel. The carburetor jets clog with varnish and fuel cannot reach the cylinder.

Other frequent causes are a fouled spark plug, dirty air filter, or stale gasoline that has lost its volatility.
symptoms: May fire briefly with starter fluid

fixSteps.title: Drain old fuel
fixSteps.instruction: Empty fuel tank and refill with fresh ethanol-free gas.

fixSteps.title: Replace spark plug
fixSteps.instruction: Remove plug, gap a new one to spec (typically 0.030 in), install.

fixSteps.title: Clean carburetor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove carb, soak in cleaner, blow out jets with compressed air.

whenToCallPro: If carb rebuild does not restore start, compression test or magneto test is needed.
videoSearchQuery: Briggs Stratton wont start carburetor clean

faq.a: Always — Sta-Bil or similar prevents varnish during storage.

title: Engine runs rough or misfires
shortDescription: Engine starts but runs unevenly with hesitation or misfire.
fullDescription:
Rough running typically indicates partial fuel restriction or ignition weakness. Most often a partially clogged main jet or a spark plug at the end of life.

Less commonly: vacuum leak at the carburetor gasket or weak coil.

fixSteps.title: Clean carb jets
fixSteps.instruction: Spray carb cleaner through main and pilot jets.

faq.a: Use ethanol-free regular for small engines.

title: Engine RPM hunts up and down
shortDescription: Engine speed cycles between fast and slow at idle.
fullDescription:
Surging is the classic symptom of a partially clogged pilot jet or carb emulsion tube. The governor opens the throttle, fuel runs out, RPM falls, governor closes, fuel returns, repeat.

A thorough carb cleaning resolves nearly all cases.

fixSteps.title: Remove and clean carb
fixSteps.instruction: Take carb off, soak overnight, blow out all passages.

whenToCallPro: If new carb does not resolve.

faq.a: Often cheaper to install a new $25 aftermarket carb.

title: Blue smoke from exhaust
shortDescription: Engine burns oil, producing blue exhaust.
fullDescription:
Blue smoke means oil is entering the combustion chamber. Most common on older engines with worn rings, but tipping the unit on its side can also cause oil migration past the rings.

Over-filled crankcase, breather failure, or worn valve guides are other culprits.

fixSteps.title: Check oil level
fixSteps.instruction: Drain to correct level if overfilled.

fixSteps.title: Run engine to clear
fixSteps.instruction: If just tipped, run 10-15 minutes to burn off residual.

fixSteps.title: Compression test
fixSteps.instruction: Check compression — under 60 PSI suggests rings.

whenToCallPro: If compression is low — engine rebuild.

faq.a: 10-30 minutes if just tipped; permanent if rings are worn.

title: Black smoke from exhaust
shortDescription: Engine running rich, producing sooty exhaust.
fullDescription: Black smoke indicates excess fuel — typically a stuck choke, dirty air filter, or a flooded carb due to a stuck float.

fixSteps.title: Verify choke operation
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm choke fully opens after warmup.

whenToCallPro: If carb float requires professional rebuild.

faq.a: Lubricate with a small dab of dry lube.

title: Oil alert system shut down engine
shortDescription: Low oil sensor stopped the engine.
fullDescription:
B&S engines with the Oil Alert system kill the ignition when oil level is below safe operating range. This protects the engine from spinning a rod bearing.

Check oil with engine on level ground; refill to full mark with correct grade.

fixSteps.title: Check oil
fixSteps.instruction: Pull dipstick, top up to full mark with SAE 30 or 10W-30.

whenToCallPro: If oil is full and sensor still trips.

faq.a: SAE 30 above 40 deg F, 10W-30 for variable temps.

title: Engine has no spark at the plug
fullDescription: When a known-good plug shows no spark, the issue is in the magneto coil, kill switch, flywheel key, or wiring. Test with the plug grounded against the engine while pulling.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect kill wire
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the kill wire from coil and test for spark.

fixSteps.title: Check air gap
fixSteps.instruction: Set coil-to-flywheel gap with a business card (~0.010 in).

whenToCallPro: If flywheel key is sheared — flywheel removal needed.
videoSearchQuery: Briggs Stratton no spark fix coil

faq.a: Yes — primary 1-2 ohms, secondary 5-10k ohms typical.

title: Engine running too hot
fullDescription:
Air-cooled engines depend on free airflow over the cylinder fins. Grass and debris packed into the shroud cause overheating and possible warpage of head gasket.

Clean fins thoroughly and check for damaged shroud.

fixSteps.title: Clean fins
fixSteps.instruction: Brush and blow out grass from cylinder fins.

title: Engine difficult to start
shortDescription: Engine eventually starts but takes many pulls.
fullDescription: Hard starting is usually low compression, a weak spark, or a slightly clogged carb. Check primer bulb is intact and producing fuel.

title: Fuel leaking from carburetor
shortDescription: Gas drips from carb bowl or vent.
fullDescription: A stuck float allows continuous fuel flow that overflows the bowl through the vent. Ethanol-related deterioration of the float needle is the usual culprit.

fixSteps.title: Tap bowl
fixSteps.instruction: Lightly tap carb bowl with screwdriver handle to free float.

fixSteps.title: Replace needle and seat
fixSteps.instruction: Disassemble carb, install new float needle.

videoSearchQuery: Briggs Stratton fuel leak carburetor float

faq.a: Yes — shut fuel valve when storing to prevent leaks.
